ITA-9.6.187 sthagikābandhaḥ स्थगिकाबन्धः
Stump bandage
A type of bandage used for the tip of the thumb, finger or penis.

ITA-3.16.38 sthapanī (marma) स्थपनी (मर्म)
Vulnerable point located near the glabella (area between eyebrows)
One in number which when injured by a foreign body may lead to death if it is removed.

ITA-4.6.10 sthānasamśrayaḥ स्थानसंश्रयः
Stage of a dosha localizing outside its location
The fourth stage of disease manifestation, when aggravated and migrant dosha lodges in a different location from its original one and gives rise to prodromal symptoms.

ITA-4.8.13 sthānāntaragatadoṣaḥ स्थानान्तरगतदोषः
Displaced dosha
Aggravated dosha which has migrated or been relocated from its original site. Synonym: āgantu-dosha.

ITA-4.8.14 sthānikadoṣaḥ स्थानिकदोषः
Correctly located dosha
Dosha residing in its own place.

ITA-1.7.28 sthāpanā स्थापना
Proving the proposed hypothesis
Justifying a proposition based on sound reason, illustration and conclusion.

ITA-3.13.20 sthālakam स्थालकम्
Head of the rib

ITA-3.13.21 sthālakārbudam स्थालकार्बुदम्
Tubercle of the rib

.12 sthālīpākaḥ स्थालीपाकः
Cooking in a vessel

ITA-5.72.2 sthāvaraviṣaḥ स्थावरविषः
Vegetable poison
Poisoning characterized by fever; hiccups; tenderness or sensitive teeth/dental hyperaesthesia; choking sensation in throat; frothy vomiting; restlessness; breathlessness/difficulty in breathing; syncope or swooning.

ITA-9.7.10 sthāvaraviṣaadhiṣṭhānam स्थावरविष-अधिष्ठानम्
Substrata of poison in plants and minerals
The various sites at which poisons are located in plants such as the root, leaf, fruit, flower, bark, pith, gum, latex, petal or bulb.
